title: Britain and Russia Split Persia into Spheres and End the Great Game
dek: On 31 August 1907 the two empires sign a convention in St Petersburg that divides Persia into a Russian north, a British southeast and a neutral middle. Tehran is not consulted.
body: The same convention settled Afghanistan and Tibet, ended decades of rivalry in Central Asia and lined Russia up with Britain and France.

panels.label: London and St Petersburg Said
panels.text: Grey and Izvolsky said the deal settled their Asian quarrels by agreement, and its text pledged to respect Persia's integrity and independence and equal trade for all nations.

panels.label: Tehran Said
panels.text: Persia's government said a pact signed without it threatened the country's integrity and refused to recognize it; nationalists who had looked to Britain turned against it.

panels.label: The Stakes
panels.text: Both empires spoke of peace and order in Asia; at stake was who would hold Persia's concessions, customs revenue and roads toward India: the two powers or the Persians.
